# Reproducible reports with Quarto {#sec-m5-quarto}

::: {.callout-warning}
## This chapter is not reproducible as it stands

It is a syntax reference, not an example to run from start to finish. The document snippets
refer to objects that are not created here (`serie`, `mapa_fluxos`, `tku`), the example
table has hand-typed numbers, and the files `modelo-mt.docx` and `referencias.bib` do not
exist in the repository. Copying a snippet into a `.qmd` and rendering it will give an error.

To see Quarto working from start to finish, use the course's complete reports: the
Paranaguá one (@sec-relatorio-paranagua), the parameterised template (@sec-m5-parametrizados) and the
final project (@sec-m5-projeto), which comes right after.
:::

A reproducible report is a document in which text, code and results live in the same
file. When the data change, the whole document updates: tables, charts, maps and the
numbers quoted in the middle of sentences.

It is the difference between "redoing last year's report" (a week of work, with the risk of
forgetting to update a number) and "running it again" (ten minutes). This site is itself a
Quarto document.

## Anatomy of a document

A `.qmd` file has three ingredients:

````
---
title: "Logistics profile of Paranaguá"
author: "Undersecretariat for Development and Planning"
date: today
lang: en
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    code-fold: true
  docx: default
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
---

## Introduction

The port handled **`r knitr::inline_expr("round(tku, 1)")` billion t·km** in 2025.

```{{r}}
#| label: fig-serie
#| fig-cap: "TKU over time"
ggplot(serie, aes(ano, tku)) + geom_line()
```
````

1. **YAML header**, between `---`: title, authorship, output format and execution options.
2. **Markdown text**, with inline code to quote numbers in the middle of a sentence.
3. **Code blocks**, which run and insert the result.

## Execution options

The most useful ones, in the YAML (they apply to the whole document) or in the block (they apply only to it):

| Option | Effect |
|:--|:--|
| `echo: false` | hides the code, shows the result: the default for institutional reports |
| `eval: false` | shows the code without running it |
| `include: false` | runs without showing anything (to prepare data) |
| `warning: false`, `message: false` | hides package warnings and messages |
| `code-fold: true` | shows the code folded, so the reader can open it |
| `cache: true` | stores the result; does not rerun if the code has not changed |
| `freeze: auto` | reruns only when the file changes (what this site uses) |

```{r}
#| eval: false
# in the block, the syntax uses #| at the start of the line
#| label: tbl-resumo
#| tbl-cap: "Summary by cargo profile"
#| echo: false
```

## Figures, tables and cross-references

Quarto numbers and references automatically, as long as the label follows the convention:
`fig-` for figures, `tbl-` for tables, `sec-` for sections, `eq-` for equations.

````
```{{r}}
#| label: fig-fluxos
#| fig-cap: "Coastal shipping flows in TKU"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
mapa_fluxos
```

As @fig-fluxos shows, the North–Southeast corridor concentrates...
See also @tbl-corredores and @sec-m5-mapas.
````

The numbering adjusts itself when you insert a figure in the middle of the document. That
eliminates the manual review of "Figure 7 (see Figure 12)" that every long report has.

## Tables

```{r}
library(dplyr)

resumo <- data.frame(
  perfil = c("Granel Líquido e Gasoso", "Carga Conteinerizada",
             "Granel Sólido", "Carga Geral"),
  tku_bi = c(157.2, 76.0, 46.1, 7.7),
  part = c(0.548, 0.265, 0.161, 0.027)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-knitr
#| tbl-cap: "With knitr::kable, simple and enough in most cases"
resumo |>
  dplyr::mutate(part = scales::percent(part, accuracy = 0.1)) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Profile", "TKU (billion t·km)", "Share"),
               align = "lrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-gt
#| tbl-cap: "With gt, when the table is the product"
resumo |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = tku_bi, decimals = 1) |>
  gt::fmt_percent(columns = part, decimals = 1) |>
  gt::cols_label(perfil = "Cargo profile", tku_bi = "TKU (billion t·km)",
                 part = "Share") |>
  gt::tab_source_note("Source: ANTAQ, Estatístico Aquaviário (TB6.1), 2025.") |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = 12)
```

`kable` handles day-to-day needs; `gt` comes in when the table needs fine formatting: groups,
footnotes, conditional highlighting, totals.

## Numbers in the middle of the text

This is the feature that prevents the most errors in institutional reports: instead of typing the number,
you compute it.

```{r}
tku_total <- sum(resumo$tku_bi)
maior <- resumo |> dplyr::slice_max(tku_bi, n = 1)
```

The text below is written like this, and if the data change, it changes with them:

````
Coastal shipping moved `r knitr::inline_expr("round(tku_total, 1)")` billion t·km in 2025,
with `r knitr::inline_expr("maior$perfil")` as the dominant profile, at
`r knitr::inline_expr('scales::percent(maior$part)')` of the total.
````

And it reads like this:

> Coastal shipping moved `r round(tku_total, 1)` billion t·km in 2025, with
> `r maior$perfil` as the dominant profile, at `r scales::percent(maior$part)` of the total.

## Output formats

```yaml
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-title: "Contents"
    code-fold: true
    embed-resources: true      # a single file, to send by e-mail
  docx:
    reference-doc: modelo-mt.docx   # applies the organisation's visual identity
  pdf:
    documentclass: scrreprt
    papersize: a4
    geometry: margin=2.5cm
    lang: en-GB
```

`reference-doc` deserves a mention in the Ministry's context: you format **once** a
`.docx` file with the official styles (font, colours, header, numbering) and every
report comes out with that identity, with no manual work.

```{r}
#| eval: false
quarto::quarto_render("relatorio.qmd")                    # every format in the YAML
quarto::quarto_render("relatorio.qmd", output_format = "docx")
```

## Structure of a report project

```
relatorio-paranagua/
├── relatorio.qmd            # the document
├── _quarto.yml              # shared options (if there are several)
├── R/
│   ├── funcoes.R            # functions, loaded with source()
│   └── 01-preparar-dados.R  # the heavy processing, run beforehand
├── dados/
│   └── processado.rds       # the data ready for the report
├── referencias.bib
└── modelo-mt.docx
```

The separation matters: the report should **not** contain the heavy processing. It reads already
processed data and focuses on presenting. That way the document renders in seconds, and the
processing (which takes minutes) only runs when the source data change.

## Citations and bibliography

```yaml
bibliography: referencias.bib
csl: associacao-brasileira-de-normas-tecnicas.csl   # ABNT, the Brazilian standard
```

In the text, `[@antaq2025]` produces the citation and builds the reference list at the end,
automatically, in the chosen style. The `.bib` file can be exported from Zotero or
Mendeley.

## Highlight blocks

The coloured blocks on this site are `callout`s: `note`, `tip`, `warning`, `important`,
`caution`. In a technical report, they serve to separate assumptions, limitations and recommendations
from the body of the text.
:::

````
::: {.callout-warning}
## Limitation
The tonnage is estimated from the TKU and straight-line distances.
:::
````


## From document to website

When the reports become a collection (one per quarter, one per corridor), the natural step
is to publish them as a website, exactly like this material. `_quarto.yml` defines the navigation, and
GitHub Pages hosts it free of charge. It is the same toolkit, at a different scale.
